items.q: The chart shows DT's usual pattern of inventory control. Calculate how much inventory DT uses each day.
items.why: Inventory falls from 6,000 to 750 units, 5,250 units, over 15 days. 5,250 ÷ 15 = 350 units a day.

items.q: A business has inventory of £145,000, total current assets of £870,000 and current liabilities of £320,000. What is its current ratio?
items.why: Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities = £870,000 ÷ £320,000 = 2.72:1. Inventory is already part of current assets, so it is not taken off.

items.q: Non-current assets £100m, CA £40m, CL £30m, NCL £20m, Shareholders' funds £50m. Current ratio?
items.why: Current ratio = CA / CL = 40/30 = 1.33:1. Ignore non-current assets, NCL, and shareholders' funds for the current ratio. Only CA and CL matter.

items.q: Wot plc (£m): non-current assets 38, current assets 31, current liabilities 18, non-current liabilities 24. It raises £20m from selling shares and uses it to buy machinery (£15m), pay off its overdraft (£3m) and increase inventory (£2m). Calculate its current ratio after these changes.
items.why: Current assets: 31 + 20 (cash in) – 15 (machinery) – 3 (overdraft repaid) = 33. Buying £2m of inventory swaps cash for inventory, so current assets stay at 33. Current liabilities: 18 – 3 = 15. Current ratio = 33 ÷ 15 = 2.2:1.
items.label: Paper 1 June 2023 Q17

items.q: A business has a 25% share of a market. The market grows by 10% and the business's sales stay the same. What is its new market share?
items.why: Take the market as 100 before the change. The business sells 25. The market becomes 110. New share = 25 ÷ 110 × 100 = 22.7%.
items.label: New question

items.q: A product sells for £15. Variable cost per unit is £10 and fixed costs are £11,000. What is the break-even output?
items.why: Contribution per unit = price – variable cost = £15 – £10 = £5. Break-even output = fixed costs ÷ contribution per unit = £11,000 ÷ £5 = 2,200 units.
items.label: New question

items.q: An investment costs £300,000. Net cash flows: Year 1: £120,000 (discount factor 0.952); Year 2: £80,000 (discount factor 0.907); Year 3: £90,000 (discount factor 0.864). What is the net present value?
items.why: Present values: £120,000 × 0.952 = £114,240; £80,000 × 0.907 = £72,560; £90,000 × 0.864 = £77,760. Total = £264,560. NPV = £264,560 – £300,000 = –£35,440. A negative NPV means the project does not cover its cost at this discount rate.
items.label: New question

items.q: Revenue £12m, Cost of sales £4m, Other expenses £3m, Taxation £2m. Operating profit = ?
items.why: Operating profit = Revenue - Cost of Sales - Other Expenses = 12 - 4 - 3 = £5m. Taxation is deducted after operating profit to calculate profit for the year. Operating profit = gross profit - operating expenses.
